entities.summary:
Ferdinand August von Lobkowicz (1652-1715) was a Bohemian nobleman and politician who played a crucial role in the governance of the Habsburg Empire.



He was born into the Lobkowicz family, a prominent noble family in the Holy Roman Empire, and after 1677, he was appointed Duke of Sagan, a significant territory in Bohemia.



Ferdinand August's tenure as Duke was marked by several key events, including the Great Northern War (1700-1721), during which he fought alongside his cousin, Emperor Joseph I, against the Swedish Empire.



His diplomatic efforts helped to secure several important treaties, including the Treaty of Prague (1708), which established a temporary peace between the Habsburgs and the Ottomans.



Ferdinand August's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Lobkowicz family on Bohemian politics and culture, as well as his role in shaping the Habsburg Empire's relations with its European neighbors.



One of the most striking aspects of Ferdinand August's life is the contrast between his family's wealth and his own relatively modest accomplishments, which has led some historians to reevaluate his reputation as a minor figure in Habsburg history.
